description: The National Forest Inventory is a rolling programme run by Forest Research that monitors woodland and trees in Great Britain and describes the size, distribution, composition and condition of forests and woodlands and how they change over time. It publishes inventory reports with quantitative estimates of stated accuracy on woodland extent, structure, composition, condition, biodiversity and social use, including tree cover outside woodland; forecast reports on how woodland may change under alternative management scenarios; reports on the scale and impact of natural events such as storms and pest and disease outbreaks; and the digital NFI woodland map, which can be downloaded from the Forest Research open data page or used through Web Map Services. Content is free under the Open Government Licence v3.0 unless otherwise stated. Caveats: inventory figures are estimates with a quoted accuracy, and forecasts depend on the management scenarios chosen. Coverage is England, Scotland and Wales. It supports green infrastructure mapping, storm damage and vegetation management studies near power lines and railways, and climate adaptation; related records are the Forestry Commission Land Information Search and the Copernicus tree cover layer.
